chapter: Joining Carter and Goodman in New York
title: Leaving Chicago to join Benny Carter in New York
summary: Hinton remembers local musicians marveling that Wilson was going to New York; they trade talk of Keg Johnson, Cab Calloway and how Hinton followed.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I remember that -- I remember that very well, that's where I came in, because you were out there and I had yet to meet you and Keg Johnson, who was my dear friend, one of the dearest friends I ever had in life, and I remember the fact that you were in New York to join Benny Carter, and it was the talk of Chicago -- Teddy Wilson is going to New York! You know, all the local musicians were saying, man, he finally made it!
We tried to get Bud, in, too, because Kay and I, like I was like the third Johnson brother, because we did get each other gigs and look out for one another.
Well, Keg got me with Cab Calloway, that's how I got out of Chicago. How I got to New York, and he told -- Keg worked with Cab Calloway.
No, Keg was with Benny Carter.
Right. When Keg later went with Cab, and then I went with Willie Bryant.
Right, and Cab went to California to make a picture with Al Jolson, and Al Morgan, his great bas$ player ...
Oh yeah, I remember the band then.

And he stayed out in California to join Les Hite and Lionel Hampton. And Keg Johnson, and now you gone and Budd was out, and Keg was trying to get me out, and he said, well, if you're looking for a bas$ player you got to go through Chicago, get Milt -- and this was my entree.
It took '35, '36 before somebody sent for me.
But we were all involved in this. So you came with -- how did Ben know about you?
